Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 45, English)
Surya Vigyan Part Two: The Maha Sookshma Sharir , and Why Maya Keeps You Fr om Claiming It

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn Mool T atva satsang continuing the ongoing "Surya V igyan" (solar science) series — intr oducing the concept of a person's own "Maha Sookshma Sharir" (Gr eat Subtle Body), why up to five such bodies can exist per person acr oss past lives, why maya specifically pr events most people fr om ever fully committing to one, and closing with Bhaiya's own extended personal account of doubt, family pr essur e, and eventual pr oof during his sadhna years.
1. Recap and Today's Dir ection

1. Bhaiya briefly r ecaps the ongoing series — the stages of bhakti, how energy forms and br eaks bonds, and the "Surya Vigyan" theory intr oduced in the prior session (r eceived, per this teaching, dir ectly fr om his own guru) — befor e continuing today specifically into Surya Vigyan's next part. 2. He explicitly notes this material is complex and states his intention to teach it gradually acr oss multiple sessions rather than all at once, encouraging the sangat to r evisit the pr evious Mool Tatva video if the foundational concepts feel unclear .
2. Even Hanuman Ji Was Tested — Devtas Keep Their Own "Hope" in a Devotee

1. Bhaiya opens with an illustrative question: why was Hanuman Ji Maharaj tested by Surasa during his journey to Lanka, given that his success was alr eady scripturally certain and sanctioned by Bhagwan Ram himself? His answer: devtas themselves maintain a kind of ongoing hope/expectation (asha) in a devotee's continued effort — this expectation is not unconditional or eternal. 2. A supporting analogy: just as par ents eventually lose hope in a child who consistently r efuses to listen or improve, devtas, saints, and mahatmas similarly maintain hope in a devotee only up to a point — r einfor cing that devotional standing must be continuously earned, not assumed as permanent r egardless of effort.
3. Intr oducing the Maha Sookshma Sharir (Great Subtle Body)

1. This teaching's central new concept: alongside a person's ordinary subtle bodies, ther e exists one (or mor e) "Maha Sookshma Sharir" (Gr eat Subtle Body) specifically and personally connected to that individual — but this entity does not help constantly; it typically intervenes only at critical, last-r esort moments, specifically when a person is on the verge of a genuine br eaking point. 2. This teaching states people commonly misattribute this r escue to whichever devta they alr eady personally know and worship (Hanuman Ji, Bholenath, Ganesh, and so on) — simply because that's the only r eference point available to them — when the actual intervention often comes specifically fr om their own personal Maha Sookshma Sharir instead.
4. The Maha Sookshma Sharir's Real Authority and Leverage

1. This teaching illustrates the Maha Sookshma Sharir's r eal leverage with an example: if this entity per ceives a thr eat to "its own person," it can dir ectly warn the local governing authority in that specific astral location that serious consequences will follow if harm comes to the person it is personally connected to — demonstrating that this is a dedicated, personal r elationship, not a generic, impersonal blessing.
5. The Distinctive "This Is Mine" Recognition Experience

1. This teaching describes a very specific, unmistakable feeling that signals a genuine encounter with one's own Maha Sookshma Sharir: an intense, immediate sense of deep familiarity and belonging ("this is definitely mine") — differ ent from ordinary attraction, and often difficult to fully explain in words. 2. This teaching states such r ecognition moments occur a limited number of times acr oss a person's life — typically up to five such instances, tied to the number of distinct Maha Sookshma Sharir a person may carry .
6. Multiple Maha Sookshma Sharir Across Past Lives — The "Anshu" Case Study

1. This teaching walks thr ough an extended, illustrative case study (continuing use of "Anshu" fr om a prior session) to explain how a single person can accumulate several distinct Maha Sookshma Sharir acr oss separate past lives: in one life, "Anshu" was a devoted bhakt who lived and eventually passed away at Ashaeiynn, leaving behind a subtle body that r emained specifically in Hanuman Ji Maharaj's service. 2. In a second life, the same soul was r eborn as "Anshul," a boy who played cricket his entir e life with total devotion, leaving behind a subtle body specifically connected to cricket. 3. In a third life, the same soul was r eborn into an Italian household and became devoted to salsa dancing, leaving behind a third subtle body specifically connected to that art form. 4. This teaching clarifies that of these thr ee (or mor e) subtle bodies, only the most r ecently active, curr ently "awakened" one r emains the true Maha Sookshma Sharir at any given time — the others r emain connected but dormant, since only one subtle body per person can be fully "awake" and active at once.
7. How Recognition Plays Out — and Why Maya Pr events Full Commitment

1. This teaching describes how , in a later incarnation, "Anshu" might encounter a person or activity connected to any one of these past subtle bodies (meeting Bhaiya/Ashaeiynn again, meeting a cricket-playing friend, meeting a salsa-dancing partner) and experience the same intense "this is mine" r ecognition each time. 2. This teaching's central caution is that a person typically fails to fully commit to any single one of these opportunities acr oss a lifetime, drifting instead between several of them without ever truly claiming one — and this exact pattern of universal-feeling-yet-never -fully-claimed is, in this teaching's own framing, pr ecisely what maya (illusion) fundamentally is. 3. A cross-r eference to a pr evious session's "four strikes" principle: consistently choosing one specific subtle body over the others (r epeatedly declining/"kicking away" the competing ones at each opportunity) allows that one entity's full accumulated prior -life siddhi and energy to accrue behind the practitioner — but this teaching states human life is specifically structur ed such that most people falter and get distracted at pr ecisely this critical junctur e, which this teaching frames as God's own "maya" at work.
8. A Live Illustration: Bhaiya's Own Maha Sookshma Sharir , Connected to Many

1. As a hypothetical illustration (explicitly caveated by Bhaiya as not a literally confirmed number), he describes his own Maha Sookshma Sharir as potentially connected to a very large number of people (illustratively , "ten lakh") — each of whom encounters and connects with that same shar ed entity at their own personally designated life-moment. 2. This teaching applies the physical principle that "energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only converted fr om one form to another" to this spiritual context: a person who fully and consistently commits to drawing fr om their own Maha

Sookshma Sharir can, in principle, draw upon the combined accumulated energy of every other person historically connected to that same entity — effectively rising above that entir e collective's level. 3. This teaching notes that this same underlying structural principle — knowingly or not — is used acr oss various religious traditions, tantra practices, and organizations (the Illuminati is specifically mentioned as an example), differing mainly in whether practitioners consciously understand the actual mechanism at work; Bhaiya states his own guru taught him this mechanism dir ectly and explicitly .
9. Practical Personal Implication: Use Your Own Maha Sookshma Sharir's Specific Pr eferred Mantra

1. This teaching's key practical takeaway: because a given person's specific Maha Sookshma Sharir has its own specific preferred mantra or name (illustrated, for this particular sangat, as "Jai Siyaram," given their specific connection to Bhaiya and Hanuman Ji Maharaj), other people's differ ent methods or mantras will simply not work as effectively for that individual, r egardless of how well those methods work for others. 2. A direct reassurance offer ed: this specific connection, once genuinely and fully embraced thr ough consistent dedication, reliably works for that individual specifically — irr espective of whether the same appr oach appears to "work" for anyone else ar ound them.
10. Ongoing Vigilance Requir ed — Maya's Pull Can Recur

1. This teaching cautions that even after a genuine connection to one's Maha Sookshma Sharir is established, the same maya-driven pull toward abandoning it can r ecur later — meaning continued attentiveness and consistent practice remain necessary rather than assuming the connection, once made, is permanently secur e without further effort.
1 1. Connecting This to Classical Hindu Philosophical Schools

1. This teaching links its framework to two long-standing devotional ideologies within Hinduism: the Vaishnav ideology , illustrated thr ough a dr op of water merging fully into the ocean and losing its separate identity/importance entir ely once merged; and the Shaiva ideology , illustrated thr ough a parr ot that r eturns to its home tr ee among many other parr ots — remaining r ecognizably itself, never merging into or becoming the tr ee itself. 2. This is connected to the br oader philosophical distinction between Advaita (non-dualism) and Dvaita (dualism), with an additional clarification (cr oss-r eferenced to a pr evious day's teaching) that Shaiva-oriented practitioners r etain shakti within themselves personally , while Vaishnav-oriented practitioners place shakti within their worshipped deity instead.
12. Bhaiya's Personal Account: Sever e Doubt and Family Pr essure During Sadhna

1. Bhaiya shar es an extended personal account of his own sadhna years: he committed r oughly 10 hours daily to practice, but when his guru eventually instructed him to begin performing hawan (which r equired money), his family — who had expected him to become a doctor or complete his PhD — r efused to support the expense and r epeatedly told him he was wasting his time, money , and life. 2. He describes an extended period of genuine self-doubt, including specifically fearing he might be "hallucinating" or suffering a psychological disorder — since he could clearly see his guru standing befor e him, yet r eceived no external, verifiable pr oof for a long time; family members and his own inner voice both suggested he might need medical/psychiatric help. 3. Despite this, Bhaiya states he continued his practice r egardless, r easoning that even if it truly was hallucination, the felt presence and connection wer e meaningful enough to be worth continuing for .
13. The Eventual, Dramatic Fulfillment of Pr oof

1. This teaching states that Bhaiya's guru eventually pr ovided overwhelming, undeniable pr oof thr ough a series of extraordinary events — including "vaani siddhi" (speech itself becoming pr ophetic/dir ectly effective), r eviving the dead,

and numer ous other advanced vidyas — to the point that Bhaiya states he now finds it difficult to even look his guru directly in the eye, out of overwhelming gratitude and humility r egarding the doubt he once held. 2. He notes, with some ir ony , that family members and others who once dismissed his practice as delusional now themselves sit devotedly at his own feet as followers.
14. Closing Reflection: Fast Drishti-Openings as a Mark of Past-Life Tapasya

1. Bhaiya closes by r eflecting that sangat members who experience rapid drishti-opening or quick spiritual connection early in their time at Ashaeiynn ar e, per this teaching's framework, likely benefiting fr om significant tapasya accumulated in past lives — dir ectly tying this observation back to the session's cor e Surya Vigyan concepts r egarding Maha Sookshma Sharir and accumulated past-life energy .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Devtas and saints maintain a limited, conditional "hope" (asha) in a devotee's continued effort, not an unconditional, permanent one — illustrated by Hanuman Ji Maharaj still being tested by Surasa despite his success already being scripturally certain. Every person has one or mor e personal "Maha Sookshma Sharir" (Gr eat Subtle Body) that intervenes specifically at critical, last-r esort moments — people commonly misattribute this rescue to whichever devta they already know , when it's often their own personal Maha Sookshma Sharir acting. A genuine encounter with one's own Maha Sookshma Sharir produces a distinctive, unmistakable "this is mine" recognition feeling — occurring a limited number of times across a lifetime, typically up to five, tied to how many such subtle bodies a person carries from past lives. A person can carry several Maha Sookshma Sharir acr oss differ ent past-life incarnations (illustrated via the multi-life "Anshu" case study — devoted bhakt, cricketer , salsa dancer) — but only the most recently active one remains truly "awakened" at any given time. Maya's cor e mechanism, per this teaching, is exactly this: everything can feel like "yours," yet a person typically never fully commits to claiming any single one of these connections — repeatedly drifting between opportunities rather than consistently choosing one, which is what prevents accumulating that one entity's full past-life siddhi. Fully , consistently committing to one's own Maha Sookshma Sharir allows a person to draw on the combined accumulated energy of everyone else historically connected to that same entity — per the "ener gy is neither created nor destroyed, only converted" principle; this same underlying mechanism is used, knowingly or not, across various religions, tantra practices, and or ganizations. Because each person's specific Maha Sookshma Sharir has its own pr eferred mantra/name, other people's methods won't work as effectively for someone else specifically — a practitioner must use precisely the mantra their own Maha Sookshma Sharir responds to (for this sangat, "Jai Siyaram"). Even after a genuine connection is established, maya's pull to abandon it can r ecur — ongoing attentiveness and consistent practice r emain necessary , not a one-time achievement. The Vaishnav ideology (a dr op merging fully into the ocean, losing separate identity) and the Shaiva ideology (a parr ot returning home yet r emaining itself) r epresent Hinduism's two classical devotional philosophies (Advaita vs. Dvaita) — Shaiva-oriented practitioners retain shakti within themselves; Vaishnav-oriented practitioners place shakti within their worshipped deity . Bhaiya's own sadhna years involved sever e self-doubt (including fear of "hallucinating") and family pr essure, with no external pr oof for a long time — he continued anyway , and his guru eventually provided overwhelming, undeniable proof through extraordinary vidyas. Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 45, English)
Surya Vigyan Part Two: The Maha Sookshma Sharir , and Why Maya Keeps You Fr om Claiming It
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Why does Bhaiya bring up Hanuman Ji Maharaj being tested by Surasa on the way to Lanka, when his success was alr eady scripturally certain? A: Per this teaching, the point is that devtas themselves maintain a kind of ongoing, conditional hope (asha) in a devotee's continued ef fort — this expectation is never entirely unconditional or permanent, even for someone as accomplished as Hanuman Ji.

Q2. Does that mean devotional standing, once earned, is guaranteed for ever? A: No — this teaching uses the analogy of parents eventually losing hope in a child who consistently refuses to listen or improve; devtas, saints, and mahatmas similarly maintain hope in a devotee only up to a point, so devotional standing must be continuously earned rather than assumed as permanent.

Q3. What is a "Maha Sookshma Sharir"? A: A "Great Subtle Body" — per this teaching, a personal subtle-body entity specifically and individually connected to a given person, distinct from that person's ordinary subtle bodies, which typically intervenes only at critical, last-resort moments when someone is on the ver ge of a genuine breaking point.

Q4. If someone feels miraculously r escued in a crisis and cr edits Hanuman Ji or another devta they worship, is that attribution always accurate? A: Not necessarily — this teaching states people commonly misattribute such rescues to whichever devta they already personally know and worship, simply because that's their only available reference point, when the actual intervention often comes specifically from their own personal Maha Sookshma Sharir instead.

Q5. Does a Maha Sookshma Sharir have any r eal authority or influence? A: Yes — per this teaching's illustration, if this entity perceives a threat to the person it's connected to, it can directly warn the local governing authority in that astral location that serious consequences will follow if harm comes to that person, showing this is a dedicated personal relationship rather than a generic blessing.

Q6. How would I know if I've genuinely encounter ed my own Maha Sookshma Sharir? A: This teaching describes a very specific, unmistakable feeling — an intense, immediate sense of deep familiarity and belonging ("this is definitely mine"), dif ferent from ordinary attraction and often dif ficult to fully put into words.

Q7. How many times in a lifetime does this kind of r ecognition typically occur? A: Per this teaching, typically up to five times, tied to the number of distinct Maha Sookshma Sharir a person may carry across past lives.

Q8. Can a single person have mor e than one Maha Sookshma Sharir? A: Yes — this teaching illustrates this through an extended "Anshu" case study: in one past life "Anshu" was a devoted bhakt who lived and passed away at Ashaeiynn (leaving a subtle body in Hanuman Ji Maharaj's service); in a second life, reborn as "Anshul," a lifelong devoted cricketer (leaving a subtle body connected to cricket); and in a third life, born into an Italian household and devoted to salsa dancing (leaving a third subtle body connected to that art form).

Q9. If a person has multiple Maha Sookshma Sharir from past lives, ar e they all active at once? A: No — per this teaching, only the most recently active, currently "awakened" one remains the true Maha Sookshma Sharir at any given time; the others stay connected but dormant, since only one subtle body per person can be fully awake and active at once.

Q10. So in a later life, could "Anshu" feel that same intense r ecognition toward mor e than one of these connections? A: Yes — this teaching describes exactly this: encountering a person or activity connected to any one of these past subtle bodies (Bhaiya/Ashaeiynn again, a cricket-playing friend, a salsa-dancing partner) and experiencing the same intense "this is mine" feeling each time.

Q1 1. What usually goes wr ong when someone experiences several of these "this is mine" pulls acr oss a lifetime? A: Per this teaching, a person typically fails to fully commit to any single one of these opportunities, drifting instead between several of them without ever truly claiming one — and this exact pattern (everything feeling like "yours," yet nothing ever fully claimed) is, in this teaching's own framing, precisely what maya (illusion) fundamentally is.

Q12. What is the "four strikes" principle mentioned in connection with this? A: Cross-referenced from a prior session, it states that consistently choosing one specific subtle body over the others — repeatedly declining the competing ones at each opportunity — allows that one entity's full accumulated prior -life siddhi and ener gy to accrue behind the practitioner; this teaching states human life is specifically structured so that most people falter at precisely this juncture, which it frames as God's own maya at work.

Q13. How many people might a single Maha Sookshma Sharir be connected to? A: As a hypothetical illustration only — explicitly caveated by Bhaiya as not a literally confirmed number — he describes his own Maha Sookshma Sharir as potentially connected to a very lar ge number of people (illustratively , "ten lakh"), each encountering that shared entity at their own personally designated lifemoment.

Q14. What happens if someone fully and consistently commits to their own Maha Sookshma Sharir? A: Per this teaching's application of "ener gy can neither be created nor destroyed, only converted," such a person can, in principle, draw upon the combined accumulated ener gy of everyone else historically connected to that same entity — ef fectively rising above that entire collective's level.

Q15. Is this energy-drawing mechanism unique to this particular teaching or sangat? A: No — this teaching notes the same underlying structural principle is used, knowingly or not, across various religious traditions, tantra practices, and or ganizations (the Illuminati is specifically mentioned as an example); Bhaiya states his own guru taught him this mechanism directly and explicitly .

Q16. Does it matter which mantra or name I use to connect with my own Maha Sookshma Sharir? A: Yes, significantly — per this teaching, a given person's specific Maha Sookshma Sharir has its own preferred mantra or name (for this sangat, illustrated as "Jai Siyaram," given their specific connection to Bhaiya and Hanuman Ji Maharaj), so other people's dif ferent methods or mantras will simply not work as ef fectively for that individual, regardless of how well those methods work for others.

Q17. If a mantra or method works well for someone else, does that guarantee it'll work equally well for me? A: No — this teaching of fers a direct reassurance instead: one's own specific connection, once genuinely and fully embraced through consistent dedication, reliably works for that individual, irrespective of whether the same approach appears to "work" for anyone else around them.

Q18. Once I've established a genuine connection with my Maha Sookshma Sharir , is that permanent r egardless of my futur e effort? A: No — this teaching cautions that the same maya-driven pull toward abandoning the connection can recur later , meaning continued attentiveness and consistent practice remain necessary rather than assuming permanence without further ef fort.

Q19. How does this teaching connect to the Vaishnav and Shaiva philosophical traditions? A: It links its framework to both: the Vaishnav ideology , illustrated by a drop of water mer ging fully into the ocean and losing its separate identity entirely; and the Shaiva ideology , illustrated by a parrot that returns to its home tree among many other parrots — remaining recognizably itself, never mer ging into or becoming the tree.

Q20. How does this r elate to Advaita and Dvaita philosophy? A: This teaching connects it to that broader distinction (non-dualism vs. dualism), further clarifying — cross-referenced to a previous day's teaching — that Shaiva-oriented practitioners retain shakti within themselves personally , while Vaishnav-oriented practitioners place shakti within their worshipped deity instead.

Q21. Did Bhaiya's own family support him during his years of sadhna? A: No — per this teaching, when his guru eventually instructed him to begin performing hawan (which required money), his family , who had expected him to become a doctor or complete his PhD, refused to support the expense and repeatedly told him he was wasting his time, money , and life.

Q22. Did Bhaiya ever doubt his own experiences during that period? A: Yes — he describes an extended period of genuine selfdoubt, including specifically fearing he might be "hallucinating" or suf fering a psychological disorder , since he could clearly see his guru standing before him yet received no external, verifiable proof for a long time; both family members and his own inner voice suggested he might need medical or psychiatric help.

Q23. Why did Bhaiya continue his practice despite this doubt? A: He states he reasoned that even if it truly was hallucination, the felt presence and connection were meaningful enough to be worth continuing for regardless.

Q24. Did Bhaiya eventually r eceive pr oof that his experiences wer e real? A: Yes — this teaching states his guru eventually provided overwhelming, undeniable proof through a series of extraordinary events, including "vaani siddhi" (speech itself becoming prophetic/directly ef fective), reviving the dead, and numerous other advanced vidyas, to the point that Bhaiya now finds it dif ficult to even look his guru directly in the eye out of overwhelming gratitude and humility .

Q25. What happened to the family members who once dismissed his practice as delusional? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya notes with some irony that those same family members and others now themselves sit devotedly at his own feet as followers.

Q26. Why do some sangat members experience rapid drishti-opening or quick spiritual connection soon after arriving at Ashaeiynn? A: Bhaiya closes by reflecting that such rapid openings are, per this teaching's framework, likely a sign of significant tapasya accumulated in past lives — directly tying this observation back to the session's core concepts of Maha Sookshma Sharir and accumulated past-life ener gy .
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 45 additions)

Always present the "ten lakh"-connected-people figure and any other specific numbers as Bhaiya's own explicitly caveated hypothetical illustrations, not confirmed literal statistics — preserve his own qualifying language exactly . Keep the distinction clear between a person's ordinary subtle body (sookshma sharir , covered in prior sessions) and the "Maha Sookshma Sharir" (Great Subtle Body) introduced in this session — these are related but distinct concepts, and should not be conflated. When explaining the multi-life "Anshu" case study , preserve the specific detail that only the most recently active subtle body is truly "awakened" at any given time — the others remain connected but dormant, not simultaneously active. Present the maya/four -strikes mechanism faithfully as this teaching's own framing (drifting between multiple "this is mine" pulls without ever fully committing to one) rather than generic advice about indecision. Preserve the specific mantra-personalization principle (each person's own Maha Sookshma Sharir has its own preferred mantra) as this teaching's own claim — do not present it as implying other practitioners' mantras or methods are invalid in general, only that they may not work as ef fectively for that specific individual. Present the Vaishnav/Shaiva and Advaita/Dvaita philosophical connections as this teaching's own framing of classical concepts, not as a comprehensive or definitive account of these traditions. Present Bhaiya's personal account of doubt, family pressure, and eventual proof as his own biographical reflection — of fered as inspiration and context, not as a claim that every practitioner will receive comparably dramatic proof or on a similar timeline. Keep the "devtas maintain conditional hope" teaching (illustrated via Hanuman Ji and Surasa) consistent with this teaching's broader emphasis that devotional standing must be continuously earned through ef fort, not assumed as permanent.

Surya Vigyan Part Two: Maha Sookshma Sharir par Live Sangat Interaction

Is session mein poor e teaching ke dauraan constant call-and-r esponse tha, ek galat guess ki corr ection thi, ek member ka personal testimony tha, aur ek closing theory-vs-practical exchange tha. Y eh EXHAUSTIVE transcript nahi hai — sirf genuinely valuable exchanges chune gaye hain, har ek ke saath ek italicized rationale note.
Bhaiya: Achha batao, jab koi bade sankat mein hota hai aur achanak koi cheez use bacha leti hai — jaise koi accident hote hote reh jaaye — log usko kiske naam se jodte hain?

(halka sa hansi ke saath sangat mein)

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek genuine, r eal-time misunderstanding hai — sangat member ne pichli teaching (kul devta) ke saath naya concept (Maha Sookshma Sharir) confuse kar diya, aur Bhaiya ki halke-phulke corr ection se yeh clarity milti hai ki yeh dono concepts explicitly alag hain, jo naye students ke liye bhi common confusion ho sakta hai.
Bhaiya: ...toh yeh recognition, yeh "yeh toh mera hai" wala feeling, life mein limited baar hi aata hai — paanch baar tak, jitne aapke Maha Sookshma Sharir hain utni baar .
Sangat member: Bhaiya, matlab paanch log hote hain jo humein connect karte hain?

Bhaiya: Nahi, paanch log nahi — paanch baar , yaani paanch situations ya moments jab aapko wo feeling aayegi. Log nahi hai yeh, apna khud ka jo subtle body hai wo hai jisse aap connect karte ho, alag alag janmon se.
Sangat member: Ohh, samajh gaya, sorry Bhaiya, mujhe laga log ginn rahe hain.

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek natural, genuinely common mishearing hai ("paanch baar" ko "paanch log" sun lena) — is choti si clarification se ek complex abstract concept (r ecognition instances vs. actual entities) bahut zyada crisp ho jaata hai, jo sirf r eading se utna clear nahi hota jitna is live corr ection se hota hai.

Sangat member (mahila, apni journey shar e karte hue): Bhaiya, main aapko batana chahti hoon, main teen saal tak Balaji mandir jaake regularly pooja karti thi, sirf yeh maang ke ki mujhe sahi raasta mil jaaye, sahi gyaan mil jaaye. Aur phir mujhe Ashaeiynn ke
baare mein pata chala. Jab maine yahan pehli class attend ki thi na, mujhe laga jaise wahi answer mil gaya jo main itne saalon se maang rahi thi.

Bhaiya: Dekho, yeh bhi ek tarah ka connection hai — aapka jo bhi Maha Sookshma Sharir hai, ya jo bhi aapka path hai, wo apne time pe khud reveal hota hai. Teen saal ki tapasya bekaar nahi gayi, wahi aapko yahan tak leke aayi.

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek genuinely personal, unpr ompted testimony hai jo abstract teaching (Maha Sookshma Sharir ka apne time pe r eveal hona) ko ek r eal, r elatable journey se jodta hai — teen saal ki dedicated prarthana ke baad Ashaeiynn tak pahunchna, yeh dikhata hai ki yeh teaching sirf theory nahi, logon ke r eal spiritual sear ch ka jawab bhi hai.

Sangat member (closing exchange, session ke aakhir mein): Bhaiya, theory toh samajh aa gayi poori — Maha Sookshma Sharir , ener gy wali baat, sab. Par yeh practical mein kaise pata chalega ki humara khud ka connection kaunsa hai?
